gaps.explanation: 'Complement' means to combine well with or complete something; 'compliment' means to praise.

gaps.sentence: He ___ that he would be late.
gaps.hint: '___ that ...' without a listener as object
gaps.explanation: 'Say' is used with reported content ('say that ...') without a person object; 'tell' needs one (tell me that ...).

gaps.sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
gaps.hint: all the money you receive from every source
gaps.explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.
'You're' is short for 'you are'; 'your' shows possession.

gaps.sentence: The new law will ___ every driver in the country.
gaps.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to have an influence on; 'effect' is normally a noun meaning a result.

gaps.sentence: This tooth is ___ and will probably fall out soon.
gaps.explanation: 'Loose' is an adjective meaning not firmly fixed; 'lose' is the verb meaning to no longer have.

gaps.sentence: Our team has a good ___ of winning on Saturday.
gaps.hint: pattern: have a good ___ of doing something
gaps.explanation: 'Have a chance of doing something' is the standard collocation for the likelihood of success.

gaps.sentence: The company has changed ___ logo twice.
gaps.explanation: 'Its' is the possessive form of 'it'; 'it's' means 'it is' or 'it has'. 'Its'' does not exist.
